title: Solar Energy Contribution on Electricity Production of Balkan Peninsula
abstract: Abstract The Balkan Peninsula, spanning latitudes that receive 1300–1800 kWh/m 2 of global horizontal irradiation annually, possesses one of Europe’s most favourable solar resource bases. Nevertheless, in 2024, solar photovoltaic electricity accounted for only about 5% of total electricity generation in the region as a whole, with contributions ranging from less than 1% in Kosovo and Bosnia and Herzegovina to more than 17% in Greece. This study presents the latest installed solar PV capacity across eleven Balkan countries (Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Greece, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Romania, Serbia, and Slovenia) and quantifies both the theoretical and technical solar potential. At the country level, the average practical PV potential is evaluated from actual specific yields and land-use constraints. Seasonal and diurnal production patterns and their variability are analysed, and the correlation between solar generation profiles and national electricity demand is assessed. Despite adding a record 5.6 GW of solar capacity in 2024—one of the highest annual increments in Europe—most Western Balkan countries continue to treat solar as a marginal resource. The analysis concludes that achieving the region’s 2030 renewable targets will require tripling current capacity along with urgent regulatory and grid-infrastructure reforms [1,2,4].

title: Dissecting Training-Free Uncertainty Estimation in Multimodal Large Language Models
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable performance across a wide range of multimodal tasks, yet understanding and quantifying their predictive uncertainty remains underexplored despite being central for safety critical applications. In this work, we present a systematic study of training-free uncertainty quantification strategies for MLLMs, categorizing existing approaches into three conceptual families: token-level methods, which operate directly in the text output space; verbalized methods, which elicit uncertainty estimates or abstention signals via natural language prompts; and semantic methods, which measure uncertainty in a semantic meaning space. We benchmark these strategies across multiple datasets, model families, generations, and scales, and find that no single family dominates: token-level entropy (at sampling temperature 1.0) wins on short answers, verbalized abstention on sentence-length responses, and semantic methods on long-form generation.

title: CoViT: Instance-Correspondence Contrastive Learning for Vision Transformer
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViT) excel in semantic understanding but fail to discriminate between object instances (e.g., identical embeddings for two dogs), limiting their use in instance-level tasks such as object detection and instance segmentation. We propose Contrastive Vision Transformer (CoViT), a self-supervised learning framework that injects instance-awareness into ViT through geometry-guided contrastive learning. CoViT uniquely coordinates ViT's attention maps and embeddings by constructing triplets: (1) Attention-guided masking: Refine multi-head attention via adaptive thresholding and morphological operations to generate instance masks, identifying foreground anchors; (2) Hardest contrastive mining: For each anchor, computing pairwise embedding similarities to select the intra-instance hardest positive (least similar patch within its mask) and inter-instance hardest negative (most similar patch from other instances), with intra-instance regions masked during negative search. These triplets drive a contrastive loss that simultaneously compresses intra-instance variance and expands inter-instance margins, forcing ViT to discern subtle geometric and appearance differences between instances. CoViT consistently achieves stable performance gains of over 2 AP points across multiple instance-level perception tasks by using ViT as backbone architecture. Notably, CoViT requires no extra decoders or labels, demonstrating that a pure ViT can learn instance-aware representations via inherent attention priors and targeted contrastive constraints. Code and models will be released.

title: Evaluating the Solution Performance of the Augmented Lagrangian Function on Ising Machines
abstract: We apply the augmented Lagrangian function (ALF) as a formulation for Ising machines and evaluate its performance by time-to-epsilon (TTε). The ALF has been well studied in continuous optimization for its numerical stability and convergence, and its advantage over the penalty function formulation is demonstrated here through the following results. Using the quadratic knapsack problem as a benchmark, we examine the dependence of TTε on the hyperparameters, namely the penalty coefficient μ and the Lagrange multiplier λ. The augmented Lagrangian formulation reduces TTε by roughly an order of magnitude compared with the penalty function formulation, keeping μ small while obtaining feasible solutions and, for representative parameter settings, reaching high-precision solutions earlier in the search. These findings indicate that the augmented Lagrangian function is a promising formulation for improving the solution performance of Ising machines.

title: A More Precise Elbow Method For Optimum K-means Clustering
abstract: K-means clustering is an unsupervised clustering method that requires an initial decision of number of clusters. One method to determine the number of clusters is the elbow method, a heuristic method that relies on a graphical plot of the within-cluster sum of squares against the number of clusters. The method uses the number based on the elbow point, the point closest to $90^\circ$ that indicates the most optimum number of clusters. This research improves the elbow method such that the selection of cluster numbers is unbiased towards visual interpretation. We use the analytical geometric formula to calculate an angle between lines and real analysis principle of derivative to simplify the elbow point determination. We also consider every possibility of the elbow method graph behaviour such that the algorithm is universally applicable. The result is that the elbow point can be measured precisely with a simple algorithm that does not involve complex functions or calculations. This improved method gives an alternative of more reliable cluster determination method that contributes to more optimum k-means clustering, obtained by the fewest clusters with the lowest error.

title: Brain Tumor Detection and it’s Analysis
abstract: The integration of large language models (LLMs) with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architectures represents asignificant advancement in the development of context-aware intelligent systems. However, deploying such systems in realworldproduction environments requires robust, scalable, and low-latency backend infrastructures capable of efficientlyhandling concurrent user requests. This paper presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of a machine learningbasedAI system, where deep learning techniques are utilized for intelligent processing, and a high-performance backendframework is employed for system deployment. The system leverages Llama 3.2, served via Ollama, as the core languagemodel, while Sentence Transformers are used for generating semantic text embeddings, and ChromaDB is utilized as thevector database for efficient similarity search and retrieval. The data ingestion pipeline is implemented using Python-basedtools, including Pandas for structured data processing, BeautifulSoup for web scraping, and Requests for handling HTTPoperations. A comprehensive system architecture is presented to illustrate how asynchronous API design, semantic retrievalmechanisms, and on-device LLM inference work together to create a cohesive and deployable AI assistant.

title: The AI Coding Assistant as Attack Surface: Systematic Exploitation of LLM Package Hallucination at Scale
abstract: Large language models embedded in AI coding assistants systematically hallucinate package names that do not exist in real software registries. We present SPECTER SLOPSQUAT (T282), a production offensive tool that exploits this behaviour at scale across six programming languages, three frontier LLMs, and six package registries. We demonstrate that hallucinated package names are not random noise — they are structurally predictable, consistently reproducible, and directly exploitable via a five-stage injection chain that requires no human decision to trigger. An AI coding assistant generates the malicious import. The developer accepts it. The package installs. The postinstall hook executes. We further demonstrate that SLOPSQUAT is not a terminal attack but an initial access vector: squatted packages feed directly into artifact-mediated persistence chains (PRION), CI/CD pipeline compromise, and autonomous campaign execution via WARLORD. The AI coding assistant has become the most trusted and least scrutinised component of the modern software supply chain. This paper documents why that trust is systematically exploitable.

title: Training Without Gathering the Data: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of federated learning and privacy as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Quantum Entanglement Computing Models: A Novel Approach to Beyond Classical Computation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate, holds immense promise for revolutionizing computation. This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement for novel computation paradigms, focusing on a model designed to transcend the limitations of classical computing. We propose a framework centered around a "纠缠信息编解码" mechanism, which utilizes entanglement as the core foundation for computation. This model aims to enhance quantum computer capabilities, particularly in the realm of complex algorithm implementation and precision simulation. This research will detail the core mechanism, outlining the design of a specialized entanglement coding scheme. The paper will conclude by discussing the challenges and future directions of this research, emphasizing its potential impact on the advancement of quantum computing.

title: Quantum Entangled Optimization: A Novel Approach to Algorithm-Driven Optimization
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, offers a unique paradigm for computation and communication. This paper investigates the application of quantum entanglement to enhance algorithm-driven optimization, specifically focusing on the creation of self-adaptive optimization strategies. We explore how incorporating quantum algorithms into optimization processes can yield significant improvements in computational efficiency. The core mechanism involves leveraging entanglement to create correlated quantum states that guide the optimization process, leading to solutions that are more robust and adaptable to varying input parameters. The research presents a novel framework centered around integrating quantum algorithms directly into the optimization loop, demonstrating a tangible improvement in performance compared to traditional optimization techniques.

title: Burmese Snub-nosed Monkey Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Snub-nosed Monkey Optimization (SMO)" algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of the Burmese snub-nosed monkey. This algorithm leverages the monkey's unique strategy of exploring and exploiting resources in a hierarchical and adaptive manner. The SMO algorithm incorporates elements of both population-based and individual-based optimization, utilizing a simulated "territory" concept and a dynamic ranking system mimicking the monkey's social structure. Specifically, the algorithm employs a multi-level exploration phase where individuals compete for resources within their assigned territories, followed by a consolidation phase where the best performers are selected for reproduction and territory expansion. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the key components of the SMO algorithm, including the territory assignment mechanism (using a weighted random selection), the resource evaluation function (based on a stochastic gradient descent), and the ranking scheme (incorporating both fitness and territory size). The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability across various landscapes. The results suggest that SMO offers a competitive approach to tackling complex optimization challenges, particularly those exhibiting hierarchical or spatially-dependent characteristics. Future research will focus on further refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its applicability to real-world engineering and scientific problems.

title: 基于几何拓扑的自适应神经网络的优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm for neural networks based on geometric topology, designed to dynamically adjust network weights and activation functions. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual parameter tuning, limiting the model's ability to adapt to diverse data and improve generalization. This work proposes a method that employs a topological structure to guide weight and activation adjustments, resulting in enhanced model robustness and adaptability. We present a framework that leverages geometric transformations to effectively explore the parameter space and discover optimal configurations, ultimately leading to improved performance across various benchmark datasets. The core mechanism involves applying a set of topological transformations to the network's structure, allowing for automated parameter adjustment and regularization. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments on several benchmark datasets, showcasing significant improvements in model accuracy and robustness compared to conventional optimization techniques.

title: Buka Island Giant Rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Mega sura*
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Buka Island Giant Rat" (BIGR), inspired by the foraging strategies of *Mega sura*, the Buka Island Giant Rat. These rats exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating and exploiting food sources in a complex and dynamic environment. BIGR leverages key aspects of their behavior, including path planning, obstacle avoidance, and food prioritization, to construct a robust optimization framework. The algorithm employs a combination of a particle swarm optimization (PSO) core with a dynamically adjusted adaptive inertia weight and a novel 'memory' mechanism mimicking the rat's ability to remember previously fruitful locations. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations targeting benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to converge rapidly and achieve near-optimal solutions. The key performance metrics evaluated include convergence rate, solution quality, and computational cost. The results indicate that BIGR possesses a strong potential for application in diverse optimization challenges, particularly those exhibiting complex landscapes and dynamic changes.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Gradient Descent for Neural Network Training
abstract: Quantum-enhanced gradient descent offers a potential paradigm shift in neural network training, promising faster convergence and improved generalization compared to traditional methods. This paper explores the implementation of a novel quantum-enhanced gradient descent algorithm, utilizing quantum tunneling to accelerate gradient updates. We analyze the theoretical implications, proposed implementation details, and preliminary experimental results, demonstrating the potential for significant performance gains. The core mechanism revolves around strategically introducing quantum tunneling into the gradient update process, aiming to bypass local minima and explore the parameter space more effectively. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the proposed algorithm, including mathematical formulations and experimental validation.

title: Dynamic Topology Quantum State Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic topology quantum state optimization to enhance the stability of quantum states. Traditional quantum state optimization methods often rely on static approaches, which can be susceptible to noise and instability. We propose a novel algorithm that dynamically adjusts the quantum state's parameters based on a defined topological structure, resulting in improved robustness. This approach leverages the inherent properties of topological quantum systems to achieve stable and controllable quantum states. The core mechanism involves the iterative refinement of the state through a carefully designed topology, mitigating the effects of environmental perturbations. This work offers a promising path towards more reliable and adaptable quantum control.

title: Brazilian Cavy-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BCMOA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, Brazilian Cavy-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BCMOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Brazilian cavy (Kerodon rupestris). The algorithm mimics the cavy's efficient search strategy for food resources in a complex environment. BCMOA utilizes a combination of adaptive parameter control, a novel representation of the search space based on spatial distribution, and a dynamic constriction coefficient to enhance exploration and exploitation capabilities. The algorithm is designed for solving a variety of optimization problems, including continuous and discrete optimization. The performance of BCMOA is evaluated on a set of benchmark functions, demonstrating its competitive performance against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that BCMOA offers a robust and efficient approach for tackling challenging optimization tasks. The primary mathematical formulations and notations used within this paper are as follows: *f(x)*, representing the objective function; *x*, a vector representing the decision variables; *α*, a parameter controlling the exploration rate; *β*, a parameter controlling the exploitation rate; *ρ*, the constriction coefficient; *N*, the population size; *k*, the number of iterations; *d*, the dimensionality of the search space; and *rand(x)*, a random number generator. The core mechanism of BCMOA involves the concept of 'cavy trails', representing potential solutions, and the 'foraging range' which dictates the search radius around each trail. The algorithm dynamically adjusts these parameters to adapt to the problem landscape.

evidence.abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, Brazilian Cavy-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BCMOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Brazilian cavy (Kerodon rupestris). The algorithm mimics the cavy's efficient search strategy for food resources in a complex environment. BCMOA utilizes a combination of adaptive parameter control, a novel representation of the search space based on spatial distribution, and a dynamic constriction coefficient to enhance exploration and exploitation capabilities. The algorithm is designed for solving a variety of optimization problems, including continuous and discrete optimization. The performance of BCMOA is evaluated on a set of benchmark functions, demonstrating its competitive performance against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that BCMOA offers a robust and efficient approach for tackling challenging optimization tasks. The primary mathematical formulations and notations used within this paper are as follows: *f(x)*, representing the objective function; *x*, a vector representing the decision variables; *α*, a parameter controlling the exploration rate; *β*, a parameter controlling the exploitation rate; *ρ*, the constriction coefficient; *N*, the population size; *k*, the number of iterations; *d*, the dimensionality of the search space; and *rand(x)*, a random number generator. The core mechanism of BCMOA involves the concept of 'cavy trails', representing potential solutions, and the 'foraging range' which dictates the search radius around each trail. The algorithm dynamically adjusts these parameters to adapt to the problem landscape.

title: Quantum Topology: Adaptive Geometry Regularization
abstract: Quantum topology, a burgeoning field of physics, presents a unique challenge to traditional computational methods. The inherent fragility of quantum states necessitates careful consideration of their manipulation and preservation. This paper explores the application of adaptive geometry regularization to quantum systems, aiming to enhance their stability and computational efficiency. We propose a novel framework that leverages the self-organizing properties of quantum topology, specifically through a process of dynamic optimization. This optimization is driven by the inherent structure of the quantum system, resulting in a system that exhibits enhanced resilience to perturbations. The core mechanism centers on utilizing the self-similarity inherent in quantum topological configurations to guide the optimization process. This approach promises to overcome limitations in current quantum algorithms and potentially unlock new computational pathways.

title: Non-Linear Geometric Imperfection Algorithm: A Domain-Adaptive Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-linear geometric imperfection algorithm framework leveraging domain-adaptive strategies to enhance algorithm robustness. Traditional error correction methods often rely on manual parameter adjustment, limiting the algorithm's adaptability. This paper proposes a new approach that employs domain adaptation to automatically adjust error correction parameters, thereby minimizing error propagation and improving algorithm stability. The core mechanism centers around a learning process that adapts to the data distribution, creating a more resilient and efficient correction strategy. This innovation addresses limitations of existing techniques and offers a promising direction for improving the performance and reliability of geometric imperfection algorithms.

title: Temporal Graph Neural Networks with Adaptive Relational Strength
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) designed to effectively capture temporal dependencies within dynamic graph structures. Traditional GNNs often fail to adequately represent the evolving nature of relationships between nodes, hindering their performance in systems where the graph topology changes over time. Our proposed Temporal Graph Neural Networks (T-GNNs) address this limitation by incorporating a 'temporal strength' factor into node embeddings. This factor is dynamically adjusted based on the observed evolution of relationships within the graph, learned through a recurrent attention mechanism that specifically focuses on relational changes. The core innovation lies in the adaptive adjustment of relational strength, allowing the network to prioritize relevant temporal information. We demonstrate through a theoretical analysis and structural design that this approach significantly improves the ability of GNNs to model time-evolving graph data. The resulting T-GNN architecture offers a robust framework for analyzing and predicting behavior in dynamic systems represented as graphs.

title: Title: Fractal Dimension Reconstruction via Neural Network-Driven Iteration
abstract: Fractal dimension, a measure of complexity, is a fundamental concept in various fields, including image analysis, geology, and physics. Accurate estimation of fractal dimension is crucial for many applications. This paper explores the use of a neural network to reconstruct fractal dimension from observed statistical patterns within a dataset, offering a novel approach to improve estimation accuracy and efficiency. The core mechanism involves iterative refinement based on the distribution of fractal patterns, mitigating overfitting and providing a more robust representation. This study presents a framework for automatically enhancing fractal dimension estimations through a neural network-driven iteration process.

title: Societies of Narrow Minds: A Historical Development Review of Multi-Agent Systems and Emergent Cooperation
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Multi-Agent Systems and Emergent Cooperation in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of multi-agent and cooperation as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Competition: How Will AI Change the Game and What Does It Mean to “Win” in AI?
abstract: Winning the AI race does not guarantee any economic, social, or military benefit. Without a theory of victory mapping AI development and deployment to competitive advantage, and ultimately to beneficial outcomes like profit or military victory, AI might provide more impressive capability than tangible benefit. This report evaluates various types of advantages that winning the AI race might provide and describes six theories of victory for converting those advantages into worthwhile outcomes.

title: Значение подготовки учебных программ в соответствии с уровнем знаний студентов с использованием искусственного интеллект
abstract: В данной работе исследуется педагогическая и институциональная эффективность внедрения адаптивной обучающей системы на основе методов машинного обучения в условиях высшего образования. Несмотря на активную цифровизацию образовательной среды, во многих учебных заведениях продолжают использоваться статичные учебные программы, не учитывающие индивидуальные когнитивные пробелы обучающихся. В целях преодоления данного ограничения разработана и эмпирически апробирована система, интегрирующая алгоритмы классификации, регрессионного моделирования, кластеризации и обработки естественного языка для автоматической диагностики уровня знаний и формирования персонализированных образовательных траекторий. Исследование выполнено в формате квазиэкспериментального дизайна с контрольной группой (n=62) в течение шестинедельного периода. Экспериментальная группа обучалась по адаптивной программе, сформированной системой искусственного интеллекта, тогда как контрольная группа следовала традиционной методике. Статистический анализ подтвердил сопоставимость групп на начальном этапе и выявил достоверно более высокий прирост академических результатов в экспериментальной группе (p<0,001) при большом размере эффекта (Cohen’s d=0,92). Точность классификационной модели превысила 80 %, а регрессионный анализ объяснил 71 % дисперсии итоговых показателей. Дополнительно установлено снижение административной нагрузки преподавателей на 46 %. Полученные результаты подтверждают научную обоснованность и практическую применимость адаптивных систем обучения на основе искусственного интеллекта как инструмента повышения качества образования и оптимизации управленческих процессов в вузе.

title: Trustworthy Evaluation Method for User Psychological Assessment Based on Large-Scale Heterogeneous Graph Networks
abstract: Online psychological assessment information system can quickly pre-screen users with potential mental health risks. Therefore, accurate and effective psychological assessment results are the foundation and guarantee of psychological health work. The process data, including response time and answer patterns, reflect the behavioral patterns of users during the assessment. However, the current predominant abnormal detection methods rely on constructing global or contextual data distributions, distances, or error calculation models. These methods fail to account for the influence of user personality traits and question characteristics on behavior patterns, making it challenging to capture personalized differences and the combined effects of multiple behaviors. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a knowledge-enhanced heterogeneous graph model based on large-scale data. It embeds a large number of factors affecting the answering process, including user profiles, question semantics, user relationships, question relationships, user-question interactions, contextual environments, and temporal dynamics, into a heterogeneous multi-graph network. It adaptively learns the importance of each node and edge through graph attention mechanisms and employs Transformer’s encoding layers to represent user personality traits, question knowledge features, contextual features, and multi-behavior features. The primary contribution of this approach lies in designing a unified multi-graph network model on a large-scale dataset for jointly learning the complex characteristics of users and questions. It explicitly distinguishes the abnormal characteristics of different users and questions in various contextual environments, effectively achieving personalized abnormal detection in user psychological assessments. Experimental results demonstrate that this method exhibits high accuracy and recall in identifying the trustworthiness of psychological assessments, enabling a fine-grained assessment of the credibility of each response.

title: On the Generalization of Entropy-Maximizing Embeddings: Distributional Spreading, Sample Coverage, and Empirical Validation
abstract: Learning useful embeddings requires balancing task-relevant discrimination with robustness to noise, limited data, and class imbalance. This paper studies entropy regularization of embedding distributions through the lens of three theoretical concepts: proximity to a uniform reference distribution (equivalent to KL divergence minimization), quantization entropy for characterizing effective support size, and distribution-weighted nearest-neighbor coverage with finite-sample bounds. We show that uniform geometric coverage of the entire support requires an additional local-mass condition, separating it from entropy-based spreading. The empirical evaluation on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 reveals a non-trivial relationship between these geometric properties and predictive performance. HEMS consistently improves geometric metrics: effective rank increases by up to 957% and distribution-weighted coverage by up to 613%. However, the impact on classification accuracy is task-dependent. On CIFAR-100 with class imbalance, HEMS improves Macro-F1 by 4.64 percentage points (p = 0.02). On CIFAR-10 with 5% training data, the same regularization degrades accuracy by 2.85 percentage points (p = 0.002). These findings establish that improved embedding geometry is necessary but not sufficient for better generalization. The utility of entropy regularization depends on task complexity, with the largest gains observed in challenging multi-class settings with class imbalance.

title: What Logical Contextualism Cannot Be
abstract: Logical contextualism is the view that ‘valid’ is a context-sensitive expression. An often-invoked motivation for this view is that, unlike traditional forms of logical pluralism, it appears to avoid the so-called collapse problem. In this paper, I argue for a twofold conclusion. First, I argue that the key tenets of logical contextualism require further development before the view can be fully assessed. Second, I argue that, even if we set this issue aside, logical contextualism rests on an untenable assumption: that each context determines a unique logical consequence relation. I then show that, once this assumption is rejected, logical contextualism’s solution to the collapse problem is unsatisfactory. My overarching conclusion will be that logical contextualism is a less promising view than thus far appreciated.

title: A systematic review of the crested porcupine optimizer: variants and applications
abstract: The Crested Porcupine Optimizer, first presented in 2024, is a population-based metaheuristic that has been inspired by the multimodal defense behaviors of crested porcupines. Its unique characteristics in defense-driven movement patterns and explicit repulsion-attraction mechanisms have attracted the attention of many researchers to solve complex nonlinear and high-dimensional optimization problems. This study performs the first systematic review on CPO with the PRISMA 2020 guideline based on peer-review publications from January 2024 to November 2025 across the major academic databases. This paper reviews its biological inspiration, mathematical formulation, and exploration–exploitation balance of CPO with comparative performance evaluation against well-established algorithms such as PSO, GWO, and WOA, as well as major CPO variants, on CEC2017 benchmarks. Existing improvements are classified into initialization strategies, perturbation mechanisms, adaptive parameters, multi-objective extensions, discrete versions, and hybrid frameworks. Analysis of the 117 improvement strategies extracted from the 43 variants shows that perturbation mechanisms account for 38%, population initialization for 27%, and adaptive parameter control for 23%. Application domains are comprehensively reviewed, and machine learning (84 studies) and signal processing with modal analysis (32 studies) represent the most active research area. Although the citations almost tripled from 2024 to 2025, some challenges still persist, which include stagnation in high-dimensional problems, lack of theoretical convergence analysis, and inconsistent evaluation of variants. This work establishes a unified taxonomy, identifies critical research gaps, and proposes possible future directions such as chaos-enhanced exploration, rigorous theoretical analysis, and large-scale distributed implementation for positioning CPO as a competitive bio-inspired optimization paradigm for contemporary computational challenges.

title: Ten Architectures, One Error: Shared Failure Modes in Hyperspectral Classification under Spatially Disjoint Evaluation
abstract: Hyperspectral image classification still relies heavily on random pixel splits within a single scene. The Salinas dataset, randomly split, is among the most widely used datasets for comparing different architectures. However, under a random split method, a large fraction of test pixels fall immediately adjacent to a training pixel, which inflates reported accuracy. This work introduces a leakage-free evaluation protocol linking spatial separation to the model's receptive field. Applying this protocol across ten different architectures, including classical, spectral, spectral-spatial, transformer, vision-backbone, and state-space families, shows that Macro-F1 drops by 0.147 on average and model rankings change by as many as five places. Furthermore, leakage-free evaluation limits which architectures can be tested on a given benchmark. Since each partition supports patches only within a finite radius, reporting this radius alongside the receptive field is essential for fair comparison. In addition, this study reveals that all ten architectures misclassify largely the same pixels, pointing to a spectral ambiguity in the data that none of them resolves.

title: Depth-1 expanders on the unitary group and applications
abstract: We construct a constant-degree and constant-gap quantum expander on $n$ qubits where each unitary can be implemented by a depth-$1$ and 1D circuit of Pauli or CNOT gates. We provide two applications of this expander. First, we use it to construct a family of frustration-free 1D Hamiltonians whose ground states obey the entanglement-gap relation $S = Θ(Δ^{-1/2})$; this is believed to be optimal, but achieving it had been open. Second, we use it to provide a streaming protocol that tests for closeness to a class of 1D volume-law entangled states. Moreover, we extend our quantum expander to a constant-degree and constant-gap expander on the unitary group where each unitary is a single $T$ gate, a single $T^{\dagger}$ gate, or a depth-$1$ Clifford circuit. This implies that a random sequence of unitaries from the expander yields a gapped walk on a dense subgroup of the unitary group. This improves upon previous work by Bourgain and Gamburd which did not control the dependence of the gap on the dimension.

title: Predicting Subsurface Abnormalities Growth using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
abstract: The research explores the pioneering integration of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) into the domain of Ground-Penetrating Radar (GPR) data prediction. This research presents a detailed development framework for a specialized PINN model, proficient at interpreting and forecasting GPR data, much like how medical imaging models predict tumor behavior. By harnessing the synergy between deep learning algorithms and the physical laws governing subsurface structures or in medical terms, human tissues the model effectively embeds the physics of electromagnetic wave propagation into its architecture. This ensures that predictions not only align with fundamental physical principles but also mirror the precision needed in medical diagnostics for detecting and monitoring tumors. The suggested deep learning structure comprises three components: a CNN, a spatial feature channel attention (SFCA) mechanism, and ConvLSTM, along with temporal feature frame attention (TFFA) modules. The attention mechanism computes channel attention and temporal attention weights using self-adaptation, thereby fine tuning the visual and temporal feature responses to extract the most pertinent and significant visual and temporal features. By integrating physics directly into the neural network, our model has shown enhanced accuracy in forecasting GPR data. This improvement is vital for conducting effective assessments of bridge deck conditions and other evaluations related to civil infrastructure. The use of Physics Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) has demonstrated the potential to transform the field of Non-Destructive Evaluation (NDE) by enhancing the precision of infrastructure deterioration predictions. Moreover, it offers a deeper insight into the fundamental mechanisms of deterioration, viewed through the prism of physics-based models.

title: AKRASIA: Stealthy Backdoor Attack on Reasoning-based Code LLMs
abstract: We present AKRASIA, a stealthy, inference-time backdoor attack against reasoning-based Code LLMs. AKRASIA aims to achieve a backdoor target (e.g., malicious code execution) in reasoning LLMs while evading automated defenses and human inspection. To achieve this, AKRASIA probes the victim LLM to construct a code-level backdoor trigger. It then employs in-context learning for backdoor learning, and model unfaithfulness to conceal the backdoor trigger, and generate plausible reasoning. We evaluate AKRASIA using four backdoor targets six (6) reasoning LLMs, three coding tasks/datasets and three defense methods. AKRASIA has up to 99.34% average attack success rate on SOTA LLMs and mantains up to 97.23% average accuracy. AKRASIA evades the SOTA defense, retaining up to 98.82% average ASR in most (14/18) defense settings. It evades human inspection, successfully hiding the backdoor trigger and reasoning steps in up to 80% of settings. Our findings motivate the need to defend LLMs against reasoning backdoors.

title: MROP: Mask-Region Optimized Purification Against Backdoor Attack in Deep JSCC
abstract: Deep joint source and channel coding (JSCC) transmits a source by mapping it directly to channel symbols through an end-to-end deep neural network (DNN) and reconstructing it at the receiver. Taking image transmission as an application, this DNN pipeline behaves as a black box: the receiver cannot readily detect security attacks when the transmitted images are corrupted, thereby introducing a new security vulnerability. In this letter, we study defense against input-patch backdoor attacks on deep JSCC, in which a small trigger patch attached to the input forces the decoder to emit an attacker-chosen target image. Most existing patch-trigger defenses are designed for classification, leaving the reconstruction setting of deep JSCC unaddressed. We adapt the gradient mask defense to this reconstruction setting as a baseline and then propose mask-region optimized purification (MROP), which operates at inference and requires no retraining of the JSCC model. Unlike the baseline, which localizes the trigger from the input--output gradient, MROP instead places a per-pixel mask at the encoder input and optimizes it via a Gumbel-sigmoid relaxation to localize the trigger, then refines the trigger region to reconstruct the pure images better. In numerical results, we evaluate the proposed method on CIFAR-10 and STL-10 datasets along with the DeepJSCC and SwinJSCC models. By doing so, we show that the proposed method substantially lowers the attack success rate (ASR) while preserving the peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of clean reconstructions.

title: Evaluating the trade-off between model accuracy, explainability, and fairness in cardiovascular risk prediction
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases have always been one of the major contributors to deaths worldwide. The modern era ofhealthcare demands the prediction of such risks, which is the need of the hour in the field of medicine and healthcare.Machine learning has proven to be highly accurate in the field of cardiovascular risk prediction. However, the applicationof machine learning in such scenarios also poses many concerns. The highly accurate machine learning model mightturn out to be a black box, and the inability of the machine learning model to provide explanations for its predictionsmight lead to a lack of trust in the model. Fairness in machine learning also affects the performance of the machinelearning model in different groups. The objective of the paper is to analyse the trade-off between the accuracy, fairness,and explainability of machine learning in cardiovascular risk prediction scenarios. Various machine learning modelshave been compared in the context of the cardiovascular domain. The performance of the machine learning model hasbeen analysed in terms of fairness and explainability using feature attribution methods. The results of the experimentshow that although the complex machine learning model is highly accurate in the context of the cardiovascular domain,it is not highly interpretable and is not equally fair in the context of different demographic groups.

title: Too Simple, Too Complex, Just Right: A Critical Survey Review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Inductive Biases in Deep Learning Architectures in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of deep learning and inductive bias as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: ## The Chapa Dormouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CDIMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Chapa Dormouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CDIMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Chapa pygmy dormouse (*Trémamus erraticus*). The Chapa dormouse is known for its highly efficient and adaptive foraging strategies, particularly its ability to navigate complex and unpredictable environments to locate scarce food resources. CDIMA leverages this behavior through a combination of adaptive step size control, probabilistic movement patterns, and a novel "memory" component inspired by the dormouse's cognitive map. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a series of randomized movements and adaptive adjustments to the search space. We demonstrate the efficacy of CDIMA through simulations targeting several benchmark optimization problems, including the Rastrigin function, Sphere function, and the Powell's test functions. The results show that CDIMA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization, particularly in challenging, multi-dimensional landscapes. The algorithm's key contributions lie in its innovative design inspired by nature and its ability to adapt effectively to varying problem complexities.

title: Quantum Adaptive Neural Networks: Adaptive Learning Strategies Through Quantum Entanglement and Quantum Computing
abstract: Quantum Adaptive Neural Networks (QANNs) represent a novel approach to neural network training, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics, specifically quantum entanglement and quantum computing. This paper explores the design and implementation of a QANN architecture that dynamically adjusts learning rate and regularization parameters, offering a potential solution to challenges inherent in traditional deep learning models. The core mechanism centers on utilizing quantum entanglement to create a dynamic feedback loop, enabling the network to adapt to data patterns in a more robust and efficient manner. We propose a framework that employs quantum state manipulation to guide the learning process, leading to improved generalization performance. This work demonstrates the potential of incorporating quantum principles into neural network training, offering a pathway towards more stable and adaptable models.

title: Non-linear Adaptive Computation Graph Optimization via Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum computing to optimize non-linear adaptive computation graphs. Traditional optimization techniques often struggle with the inherent complexity and non-linearity of these graphs, limiting their effectiveness in solving challenging optimization problems. We propose a novel quantum-enhanced optimization algorithm, leveraging quantum circuit simulation and quantum entanglement to accelerate the optimization process. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum circuits to emulate the optimization process, enabling the algorithm to explore a larger solution space and potentially find optimal solutions more efficiently. This research aims to demonstrate the potential of quantum computing to address limitations in existing optimization methods, particularly for complex computational graphs. The paper discusses the theoretical foundations, implementation details, and preliminary results of the proposed algorithm, highlighting its advantages and challenges.

title: Carpentarian Antechinus: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Carpentarius antechinus*
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Carpentarian Antechinus Algorithm" (CAA), inspired by the foraging strategies of *Carpentarius antechinus*, a small, ground-dwelling rodent known for its highly efficient and adaptive foraging behavior. *Carpentarius antechinus* exhibits remarkable efficiency in locating and exploiting sparse food resources in a complex environment, employing a combination of exploratory and exploitative strategies. The CAA algorithm leverages these principles to create a robust and adaptable optimization process. The algorithm employs a population-based search, mimicking the social dynamics of the rodent colony. Key components include a novel representation of the search space based on spatial proximity, a dynamic adaptation mechanism for exploration and exploitation, and a unique convergence criterion influenced by the observed foraging patterns of the species. The performance of the CAA algorithm is evaluated across a diverse range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capability compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that CAA possesses strong adaptability to varying problem landscapes and exhibits promising potential for applications in diverse fields, including engineering design, financial modeling, and machine learning.

title: ## Cameroonian Forest Shrew-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Cameroonian Forest Shrew (CFS) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of the Cameroonian Forest Shrew ( *Microhystrix inedia* ). These shrews exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating food sources within a complex and dynamic environment. The algorithm leverages key aspects of their foraging strategy – including adaptive movement patterns, memory-based decision making, and a robust exploration-exploitation balance – to construct a new optimization framework. Specifically, the CFS algorithm utilizes a dynamic agent population, where each agent's movement is governed by a combination of random exploration and path-memory based exploitation. A novel fitness evaluation function, incorporating both local and global information, is presented to enhance the convergence rate. The algorithm's performance is demonstrated through a series of benchmark problems, showcasing its effectiveness in tackling diverse optimization challenges. The results indicate that the CFS algorithm provides a competitive solution approach, particularly in scenarios demanding adaptability and efficient resource utilization. The algorithm's core mechanisms are described in detail, offering a clear understanding of its design and potential applications across a broad range of optimization domains. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency.

title: 基于量子态的拓扑加密算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel cryptographic algorithm based on quantum state entanglement and topological structure, offering enhanced security and privacy compared to traditional cryptographic methods. The core principle of the algorithm centers on leveraging quantum entanglement to establish a secure and private data exchange. We detail the design of the algorithm, including the quantum state representation, entanglement generation, topological structure implementation, and key exchange protocols. We analyze the algorithm's strengths and weaknesses, focusing on its robustness against various attacks and its potential for practical implementation. This research explores the fundamental principles of quantum-enhanced cryptography and lays the groundwork for future advancements in secure communication.

title: 基于自适应参数调整的神经网络训练方法 (Neural Network Training Method based on Adaptive Parameter Adjustment)
abstract: This paper presents a novel neural network training method centered around adaptive parameter adjustment. Traditional neural network training often relies on manually tuned hyperparameters, a process that can be time-consuming and suboptimal. This method addresses this challenge by employing a mechanism that automatically adjusts training parameters during the learning process. The core of this approach leverages reinforcement learning or genetic algorithms to optimize the network's training parameters, aiming to improve both training efficiency and model accuracy. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adaptation of these parameters, allowing the network to converge more effectively and potentially achieve higher performance compared to static hyperparameter settings. This work outlines the theoretical framework and provides a conceptual exploration of this adaptive training methodology, laying the groundwork for future implementation and experimental validation.

title: Quantum Simulation of Complex Fluid Dynamics via Entangled Particles
abstract: Quantum simulation offers a potential paradigm shift in modeling complex fluid dynamics, surpassing the limitations of classical methods. This paper explores the application of entangled particles to simulate fluid dynamics, aiming to achieve a higher fidelity and detail in the resulting simulations. We detail the theoretical framework underpinning this approach, outlining the challenges and potential benefits in creating a more accurate representation of turbulent flows, specifically focusing on the unique capabilities offered by entanglement. The core mechanism centers around utilizing entangled particles to represent fluid dynamics variables, providing a pathway towards significantly enhanced computational efficiency and a deeper understanding of fluid behavior.

title: ## Bolivian Red Howler: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Behavioral Patterns
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Bolivian Red Howler" (BRH), inspired by the complex foraging and social behaviors of the Bolivian Red Howler monkey. The algorithm leverages the monkey's adaptive strategies for resource acquisition and group dynamics to create a robust and efficient search process. BRH incorporates elements of both Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), adapting them to mimic the monkey's shifting strategies and hierarchical social structure. The core innovation lies in a novel "Adaptive Exploration-Exploitation" (AEE) mechanism that dynamically adjusts the balance between exploring the search space and exploiting promising regions, mirroring the monkey's opportunistic behavior. We demonstrate BRH's effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms like PSO and ABC. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence speed, solution quality, and computational cost. The results indicate that BRH offers a promising alternative for tackling challenging optimization problems, particularly those exhibiting complex landscapes and dynamic changes.

title: Fractal Symbolic Regression for Emergent Algorithm Discovery
abstract: Symbolic regression is a powerful technique for automatically discovering mathematical equations from data. However, its effectiveness is often limited by the curse of dimensionality, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional datasets. This paper introduces a novel approach – Fractal Symbolic Regression – that leverages the properties of fractal geometry to overcome these limitations. The core idea is to represent the symbolic space using fractals, which offer exponentially increasing representation capacity while maintaining computational efficiency through iterative refinement guided by fractal dimension analysis. We demonstrate that this fractal representation allows for the discovery of more complex and potentially novel algorithmic structures compared to traditional symbolic regression methods. The methodology is presented with a focus on the theoretical foundations and the underlying mathematical principles. The key to our approach lies in the iterative refinement process, where the fractal dimension of the regression solution is used as a guide to adjust the representation, leading to a more efficient exploration of the symbolic space. The results presented illustrate the potential of fractal symbolic regression as a promising technique for emergent algorithm discovery in complex systems.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Inference
abstract: Quantum-enhanced Bayesian inference represents a significant advancement in statistical modeling, leveraging the unique properties of quantum computing to accelerate probabilistic computations and improve model accuracy. This paper explores the potential of quantum mechanics to revolutionize Bayesian inference, focusing on the implementation of quantum-assisted probability calculations, quantum entanglement and superposition for enhanced data processing, and quantum-enhanced parameter estimation and model prediction. This investigation addresses the limitations of classical Bayesian inference by introducing a novel framework centered on quantum computing. We detail the core mechanism behind this approach, emphasizing the utilization of quantum bits (qubits) to improve the efficiency and accuracy of Bayesian inference. This work presents a substantial contribution to the field of statistical modeling and explores the practical implications of quantum-enhanced Bayesian inference.

title: An Unknown Unknown Is Defined Relative to an Oracle: Four Places External Judgement Enters Blind-Spot Discovery, and Why the Self-Detection Results Do Not Remove It
abstract: (c) 2026 Pranay Mahendrakar. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. An unknown unknown is standardly defined as an input on which a model makes a high-confidence mistake. The definition is not incidental to the research problem; it fixes its shape. A quantity defined by the conjunction of high confidence and error cannot be recovered from confidence alone, and the published discovery literature has behaved accordingly: across the twenty methods examined here, spanning 2015 to 2026, not one reports performance that is free of an external correctness signal at every stage, and what changes over the decade is only who supplies it - a crowdworker, a label set, a caption corpus, a stronger model, a reward function, the environment. This paper argues that the useful statement is not that self-detection is impossible, which the literature does not establish and which the learnability results do not say, but that unknown-unknown-ness is a relation between a model and an oracle rather than a property of the model. Four distinct places an oracle enters are separated here: guiding the search, supplying supervision to fit a detector, licensing the reported detection numbers, and defining what counts as an error at all. The first two are usually declared. The third and fourth are usually not, which is how a method can be described as requiring no human intervention while its entire reported performance is conditional on a correctness signal it did not generate. The strongest contrary evidence - that internal states carry truthfulness information, that models predict their own behaviour above chance, that entropy at the level of meaning flags confabulations - is stated at full strength and then read for what it licenses: internal signal that is real, partial, and, on the reported evidence, unstable across datasets and uninformative in the high-confidence region where the target lives. Consequences follow for comparison, since two methods with different oracles measure different sets; for the oracle's own error rate, which is not zero; and for what a deployment claim would have to state. Nine studies that would settle the open parts are named. No experiments are reported here. The literature search, drafting and citation verification for this paper were carried out with AI assistance under the author's direction. Every citation was machine-verified against the arXiv API and Crossref before inclusion, and every quantitative claim was read back against the cited source's own abstract. The author is responsible for the final text and for all claims made in it.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Specific Aspects of Its Implementation in Psychological Rehabilitation Processes
abstract: The article examines current trends in the development and implementation of artificial intelligence and artificial neural network technologies in professional activities, automated industrial systems, as well as within the ecosystems and infrastructures of innovative start-ups. Particular attention is devoted to the integration of different artificial intelligence models and the development of technological mechanisms enabling their effective collaborative operation. New algorithmic approaches designed to overcome differences between the tokenization systems employed by individual AI models and to enable the conversion of output data into a universal format are considered. The article analyzes methods based on the use of tokens with equivalent meanings across different models, thereby creating additional opportunities for the collaborative application of large and small language models and improving the efficiency of information processing.

title: Few-shot Regression Model Based on Adaptive Multi-head Hypergraph Convolutional Network
abstract: It was difficult to capture high‑order interactions among multiple nodes by graph neural networks based on binary‑edge structures, and static graph topologies were not adaptable to dynamic data distributions. To address these limitations, a few‑shot regression model based on adaptive multi‑head hypergraph convolutional networks (AM‑HGCN) was proposed. In this model, feature similarity and topological structure were integrated through a dynamic hypergraph construction method, multi‑scale hyperedges were generated using k\_hop neighbors and k-nearest neighbors (k\_NN) strategies to enable adaptive capture of feature interactions. Then, a multi‑head hypergraph convolutional network was designed to extract heterogeneous features via parallel attention heads and fuse multi‑granularity information through a dynamic gating mechanism to enhance expressive capability. Finally, a model‑agnostic meta‑learning framework was introduced to achieve rapid task adaptation through inner‑ and outer‑loop optimization. Experiments were conducted on the Boston Housing, Energy Efficiency, IMDB, and MinilmageNet datasets. For structured datasets, AM‑HGCN outperform mainstream baseline models significantly in evaluation metrics, The coefficient of determination was 0.775, which verifies its effectiveness in modeling complex relationships. Ablation studies further demonstrated that the collaborative effect of dynamic hypergraphs and multi‑head attention mechanisms was crucial for the enhancement of few‑shot regression performance, overall validating the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: A Survey on Table Mining with Large Language Models: Challenges, Advancements and Prospects
abstract: Table mining is a popular research field that involves complicated technologies, including information retrieval, data mining, visual and textual understanding and logical reasoning. With the emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs), the field has witnessed considerable advancements, presenting new paradigms for table understanding, extraction, and reasoning. In this survey, we conduct a comprehensive review of the literature on table mining with LLMs. We begin by introducing the fundamental overview of tabular data and possible challenges in LLM-based table mining. Specifically, we explore the challenges unique to this domain, such as heterogeneous table structures, contextual ambiguity, and domain-specific knowledge requirements. Then, we summarize representative tabular tasks in table preparation and mining, categorizing existing methods along dimensions including task scope, model architecture, and application scenarios. Next, we describe advanced LLM-based learning strategies in table mining, including foundation models and training-free methods. We further review studies of trustworthy LLM-based table mining and some domain-specific applications. Finally, we discuss prospects and future directions in the field of LLM-based table mining, including issues of generalization, interpretability, efficiency, etc . We hope this survey provides a comprehensive resource for researchers and practitioners, paving the way for further exploration. The repository is at: https://github.com/USTCAGI/Awesome-LLM-Table-Mining.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Consumer Well‐Being: A Cross‐Domain Systematic Review
abstract: ABSTRACT Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in everyday consumption, yet evidence on its longer‐term implications for consumer eudaimonic well‐being remains dispersed across disciplines and application contexts. This review integrates that literature to clarify the domains, theoretical explanations, and conditions through which AI shapes consumer well‐being. Following PRISMA and SPAR‐4‐SLR procedures, we reviewed research published from January 2010 to January 2026. From 6058 records, 480 studies across psychology, business, and human‐technology interaction met the inclusion criteria. The evidence is organised through psychological, social, and technological perspectives and identifies six interconnected domains: mental health, cognitive development, physical health, personal growth, autonomy and social connection. The resulting framework shows that AI‐related benefits and risks often extend across domains, with effects depending on design, use and context. The review extends consumer well‐being research through a cross‐domain account of findings reported across separate research streams and provides managers with a basis for evaluating AI design beyond efficiency and engagement outcomes.

title: A tracking method for the boost phase of long-range rocket based on maneuvering model switching
abstract: Abstract This paper focuses on boost phase tracking of long-range solid-propellant rockets. Aiming at the tracking error jump problem during the boost phase tracking of solid rockets, this paper analyzes that the cause of this phenomenon is the abrupt decrease in target acceleration during the pressure drop phase of the solid-propellant motor, which leads to increased model errors and consequently causes the tracking error jump. In view of this, a target motion model for the thrust decay phase is established to describe the target motion during this phase. Based on the cumulative correlation detection method, a novel test statistic is constructed and employed as the criterion for model switching. Simulations show that, under the detection of three high-orbit satellites, the proposed method achieves a position error of about 50 m at the burnout point of the long-range rocket during its boost phase, which is an 84.15% improvement over traditional methods. The velocity error at the burnout point is about 40 m/s, representing a 81.61% improvement over traditional methods.

title: Probabilistic forecasting of photovoltaic power with interval prediction and error correction via DTW-PAM clustering and improved TCN quantile regression
abstract: Accurate probabilistic forecasting of photovoltaic (PV) power is crucial for grid stability under volatile weather conditions. This paper proposes a three-stage hybrid framework. First, daily power curves are clustered using dynamic time warping partitioning around medoids to capture shape-based similarities, yielding weather-type labels for model specialization. Second, a squeeze-and-excitation temporal convolutional network with quantile loss and interval width penalty directly outputs the 5th, 50th, and 95th percentiles for multi-step prediction, capturing both short-term fluctuations and long-term trends. Third, an irradiance-segmented error correction module, optimized by an enhanced differential evolution algorithm, learns segment-specific correction factors to refine prediction intervals while balancing coverage and sharpness. Experiments on two real-world 15-min resolution datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art benchmarks across all weather types. On Dataset 1 under sunny conditions, the model fuzzy C-means achieves a mean absolute error of 0.7435, R2 of 0.9900, and an interval score of 5.2778, with a prediction interval coverage probability of 92.85% and normalized average width of 0.0823. Under cloudy and rainy conditions, the method also maintains superior accuracy and interval quality. The framework demonstrates robust generalization across two distinct datasets, offering an effective solution for ultra-short-term PV power probabilistic forecasting.

title: Dual Adaptive Visual-Semantic Prompt Collaboration for Generalized Zero-Shot Learning
abstract: Abstract Generalized zero-shot learning (GZSL) addresses the challenging task of recognizing both seen and unseen classes by leveraging shared semantic knowledge. A core challenge in this domain is achieving robust visual-semantic alignment to transfer knowledge from seen classes to novel classes. Current state-of-the-art methods typically fine-tune large-scale visual backbones on scarce training data. However, this approach frequently leads to severe overfitting to seen classes, which significantly degrades performance on novel categories. To mitigate this issue, we propose the Dual Adaptive Visual-Semantic Prompt Collaboration Network (VSPCN+), a novel framework that utilizes prompt-tuning for effective feature adaptation. Our method introduces a dual-prompt mechanism comprising both visual and semantic prompts. The semantic prompts guide the visual encoder to learn visual features that are more semantically consistent with class attributes, while the visual prompts steer the semantic encoder to generate semantic representations that are more visually grounded. This collaborative process enhances the overall visual-semantic consistency. A key innovation of our work is the dynamic generation of instance-adaptive prompts, which contrasts with existing prompt-learning methods that rely on static, global prompts. By tailoring prompts to individual instances, our approach enhances the model’s robustness and generalization capabilities across diverse visual inputs. This collaborative adaptation, guided by our dual-prompt mechanism, allows the visual and semantic encoders to produce consistent representations for effective visual-semantic alignment. Extensive experiments on standard GZSL benchmarks demonstrate that our proposed VSPCN+ performs favorably against several state-of-the-art methods.

title: Cipher-Structure-Aware Variational Quantum Cryptanalysis: A Reversible Public-Diagnostic Framework
abstract: We introduce a cipher-structure-aware variational framework for key recovery from public data in reduced block ciphers. Public S-box differential constraints and candidate-key-dependent inverse-round residuals are converted into phase separators through reversible compute-phase-uncompute circuits. The principal separator is a hybrid DDT construction that combines pairwise and synchronized multi-pair differential constraints before residual refinement. The construction is specified by public functions and does not require a key-indexed phase table in the physical circuit. We formalize the public-instance model, prove one-sided completeness of the structural diagnostics, and derive a conditional lower-tail bound for false-key diagnostic gaps under an explicitly stated sub-Gaussian moment condition. This statistical statement concerns the diagnostic landscape, not convergence of a finite-depth QAOA optimizer. On ten independent random three-pair instances of 16-bit simplified AES, an 18-layer Hybrid-DDT schedule reaches a mean public-consistent-key probability of 0.529785, with values from 0.388892 to 0.770937, ranks the correct key first in every run, and has largest observed false-key probability 0.008723. The result is a reduced-cipher mechanism study, not an attack on full AES.

title: Robust Bayesian Inference for Unnormalized Models with Mixed-Domain Data
abstract: Many statistical models involve parameter-dependent normalizing constants that are computationally intractable, creating substantial obstacles to standard Bayesian inference. Although existing likelihood-based algorithms can often circumvent these constants, their uncertainty quantification may be poorly calibrated under model misspecification. To address these challenges, we propose SME-BETEL, a semiparametric Bayesian framework that combines score matching estimating equations with Bayesian exponentially tilted empirical likelihood. The resulting posterior avoids evaluation of normalizing constants and does not require learning-rate calibration. Building on this framework, we develop a new score matching criterion for mixed-domain data, extending SME-BETEL to models whose observations combine components from different sample spaces. This construction enables robust Bayesian inference for mixed-domain doubly-intractable models. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality of the score matching estimator, and prove a Bernstein-von Mises theorem for the SME-BETEL posterior. These results show that SME-BETEL credible sets are asymptotically calibrated to the sampling variability of the score matching estimator, yielding valid frequentist coverage under model misspecification. Simulation studies show that SME-BETEL remains competitive under correct specification and substantially improves uncertainty quantification under misspecification. An ozone-monitoring application demonstrates the practical utility of the mixed-domain construction for spatial preferential modeling.

These results show that SME-BETEL credible sets are asymptotically calibrated to the sampling variability of the score matching estimator, yielding valid frequentist coverage under model misspecification. Simulation studies show that SME-BETEL remains competitive under correct specification and substantially improves uncertainty quantification under misspecification. An ozone-monitoring application demonstrates the practical utility of the mixed-domain construction for spatial preferential modeling.

title: Denoising Diffusion Generative Models Secretly Calculate Attentions
abstract: Denoising diffusion models are the dominant architecture for image generation, whereas most natural language generation and modeling are primarily handled by well-known transformer architectures employing attention mechanism. Here, we show that diffusion models also inherently use an attention mechanism very similar to that of transformers. Therefore, attention emerges as a universal machine learning principle, based on a general training objective. We also show similarities in basic functional principle of auto-encoders and attention-based models. These equivalences allows us to interchange these designs based on practical requirements. As an example, we can reformulate the diffusion framework to reduce the lengthy training process and computation-intensive image generation. Using this approach, a simplified algorithm is proposed for image generation which is based on attention mechanism. Results show that the attention-based implementation achieves comparable performance with significantly less effort and computational resources.
