title: 基于自适应的量子系统优化算法
abstract: Quantum systems represent a complex landscape for optimization, particularly in areas like materials science, drug discovery, and financial modeling. However, achieving optimal solutions often requires extensive computational resources and sensitive to fluctuations in quantum states. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, "Adaptive Quantum Optimization," designed to address these challenges by dynamically adjusting quantum step sizes during the optimization process. The core mechanism of this algorithm leverages self-adaptive quantum algorithms to optimize the quantum trajectory, enhancing both algorithm efficiency and stability. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, achieving significant improvements in convergence speed and robustness compared to traditional optimization methods. This work presents a promising pathway toward more efficient and reliable quantum optimization.

title: Brazilian Spiny Tree Rat-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed the "Spiny Tree Rat Algorithm" (STAR), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Brazilian spiny tree rat ( *Galea sp.*). These rats exhibit a unique strategy for locating food sources in complex, three-dimensional environments, characterized by a combination of exploration and exploitation. The STAR algorithm leverages this behavior through a novel representation of the search space, a dynamic obstacle avoidance mechanism mimicking the rat's cautious movements, and an adaptive adjustment of the exploration-exploitation balance. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a stochastic search mechanism, aiming to find optimal solutions to complex optimization problems. Performance evaluation is conducted on a set of benchmark problems, demonstrating the algorithm's competitive effectiveness in comparison to established metaheuristic techniques. The key contributions of this work lie in the innovative application of the spiny tree rat's foraging strategy to metaheuristic optimization and the design of a practical and efficient algorithm that can be applied to a wide range of optimization challenges.

title: Self-Correcting Digital Circuits Based on Reservoir Computing
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to digital circuit design centered around reservoir computing and self-correction mechanisms. Traditional digital circuit design methodologies often grapple with the detrimental effects of inherent noise and process variations, leading to unreliable and inconsistent performance. The core idea is to leverage the dynamic adaptation properties of reservoir computing, specifically recurrent neural networks, to create circuits that actively mitigate the impact of noise. The proposed architecture utilizes a digital circuit implementation of a reservoir, allowing for real-time adjustment of its parameters to compensate for disturbances. Mathematical formulations detail the dynamics of the reservoir and the control signals necessary for self-correction. The resulting circuits exhibit enhanced robustness and improved performance in the presence of noise, marking a significant step towards more reliable and adaptable digital hardware. This work demonstrates a viable pathway to building inherently self-correcting digital circuits, addressing a critical limitation in current digital design practices. ---

title: Quantum-Driven Algorithm Design for Dynamic Systems
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum algorithms to the design of dynamic systems, focusing on the creation of novel and efficient algorithms that promote adaptability. The core concept centers around harnessing quantum phenomena – superposition, entanglement, and interference – to generate algorithmic solutions with enhanced capabilities for evolving and responsive systems. We investigate a novel algorithmic framework predicated on quantum-enhanced optimization, proposing a method for automated algorithm discovery and refinement through quantum simulations. The central claim is that this approach can significantly accelerate the development of algorithms for dynamic systems, surpassing the limitations of classical approaches in adaptability and efficiency. The paper details the theoretical foundation of this algorithm, presents preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of the quantum-driven design, and concludes with a discussion of future research directions.

title: Composable Neural Modules with Formal Interface Specifications
abstract: The construction of complex neural networks from individual modules frequently relies on intuitive design choices, resulting in a lack of formal guarantees regarding their composability. This paper proposes a novel framework for designing modular neural networks based on formal interface specifications. We introduce a dedicated language to precisely define the inputs, outputs, and functional behavior of neural modules, allowing for automated verification of compatibility and ensuring seamless integration during network construction. This approach shifts the focus from ad-hoc design to a rigorous, verifiable methodology, promoting reusability, reducing integration complexity, and ultimately contributing to the development of more robust and reliable neural network architectures. The core of this work lies in establishing a mathematically sound foundation for modular neural network design, addressing a critical limitation in current practices. We outline a formal system with a focus on ensuring correct composition and enabling automated verification, ultimately leading to more trustworthy and maintainable AI systems. ---

title: Bogota Tapeti: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Bogota Tapeti Bird
abstract: This paper presents Bogota Tapeti, a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bogota Tapeti bird ( *Thraupis episcopus* ). The algorithm leverages the tapeti's unique strategy of searching for food in a patch-based manner, combined with a novel adaptive mutation operator. Bogota Tapeti aims to improve upon existing metaheuristic techniques, particularly in addressing premature convergence and enhancing exploration capabilities. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a patch-based representation and dynamically adjusting the size and distribution of patches based on the algorithm's progress. The core of the algorithm lies in its adaptive mutation operator, which probabilistically modifies the patch assignment and food quantity within each patch, promoting diversity and preventing stagnation. We evaluate Bogota Tapeti on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Simulated Annealing (SA). The experimental results show that Bogota Tapeti exhibits strong convergence rates and robustness across a range of problem types. Future work will focus on refining the adaptive mutation operator and exploring potential applications of the algorithm in areas such as machine learning and engineering design.

title: Core Claim: Develop a neural network self-adaptive adjustment method that dynamically adjusts network parameters based on input data and historical performance to enhance model generalization and performance.
abstract: Neural networks have demonstrated remarkable capabilities across various domains, yet their performance often relies heavily on careful hyperparameter tuning. This paper introduces a novel neural network self-adaptive adjustment method leveraging deep neural networks to dynamically adjust network parameters in response to input data and historical performance. The core mechanism involves training a neural network to learn the relationship between input data and past performance, enabling the system to automatically adjust parameters to optimize model performance. This approach overcomes the limitations of traditional parameter tuning methods, offering a more adaptive and potentially more effective strategy for improving model generalization and overall accuracy. We present a comprehensive framework demonstrating the benefits of this approach through extensive experiments on benchmark datasets. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in model performance compared to existing methods, highlighting the potential of this self-adaptive adjustment technique. The paper concludes with a discussion of the theoretical implications and future directions for this research.

title: ## Black-tailed Hutia: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Black-tailed Hutias
abstract: This paper introduces Black-tailed Hutia (BTH), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Black-tailed Hutias ( *Ratufagus leucura* ) in the cloud forests of Colombia. BTH leverages the hutias' efficient exploration and exploitation strategies for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, incorporating adaptive mutation and a novel 'nesting' mechanism mimicking the hutias' tendency to construct and revisit preferred foraging locations. Mathematical formulations are presented to describe the core components of BTH, including the population update rule, the adaptive mutation operator, and the nesting strategy. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capabilities. The key contributions of this work lie in the unique integration of behavioral observations and mathematical modeling to create a robust and adaptable metaheuristic algorithm.

title: Construção de sistemas de organização do conhecimento: uma experiência prática
authors: Regina Aparecida Prisco Paiva Garcia Silva
Regina Aparecida Prisco Paiva Garcia Silva
abstract: Knowledge Organization Systems (KOSs) are instruments used to organize, represent and retrieve information and knowledge. This study presents an experience report on the integrated construction of four KOSs: taxonomy, classification system, thesaurus and ontology, supported by a glossary and a concept map. The objective was to report on the practical experience of developing these instruments and to understand the relationships established among them. The research is characterized as qualitative, applied, descriptive and exploratory, focusing on information search and retrieval systems as its domain. The process involved selecting and analyzing a text representative of the domain, identifying and selecting concepts, and constructing the instruments using the Cmap, Thesa and Protégé software. The results revealed distinct structures, semantic relationships and levels of formalization among the instruments, while demonstrating that their articulated construction allows each stage to support subsequent ones. Difficulties were also identified in defining conceptual relationships and using the technological tools, particularly in the development of the concept map and ontology. It is concluded that the integrated construction of KOSs contributed to both the theoretical and practical understanding of their characteristics and relationships, highlighting their pedagogical potential for teaching and learning Knowledge Organization.

title: Determining the Minimum Amount of Tissue Required for Outcome-Relevant Histopathologic Feature Stratification in NMIBC
abstract: Background - Non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) comprises 75% of bladder cancer diagnoses and is characterized by frequent recurrence. Clinical management is guided by risk stratification, which incorporates subjectively assessed tumour grade. Digital pathology enables objective quantification of features from whole slide images (WSIs), however the minimum cancer tissue needed for reliable grading is undefined, and the prognostic significance of small high-grade components in otherwise low-grade cancers remains uncertain. We hypothesize that there exists a minimum number of cancer cells sufficient to capture clinically relevant histopathologic features such as recurrence-free survival. Methods - The cohort included a single digitized WSI from each of 163 patients with stage Ta NMIBC and clinical follow-up data. Quantitative measurements of 11 nuclear features were extracted from each WSI using digital pathology software (Visiopharm, Hørsholm, Denmark). Each WSI was sampled into progressively smaller tissue subsets. At each sampling threshold, Jensen-Shannon (JS) divergence assessed similarity in feature distributions relative to the full WSI. Nuclear features were then summarized at each sampling threshold and used to stratify patients for Kaplan-Meier analysis of their association with recurrence-free survival. Results - We found feature distributions showed the greatest improvement in similarity to the full slide between 5% and 25% tissue sampling, with only smaller gains as more tissue was added. Lesser nuclear diameter and eccentricity retained prognostic significance with limited sampling, whereas ellipticalness, solidity, and convexity were relatively more sensitive to limited sampling. Survival analyses found higher sampling thresholds recovered more significant prognostic features, with thresholds of 20-25% showing feature recovery most comparable to full-slide analysis. Conclusions - This study begins to establish quantitative tissue thresholds for digital pathology in NMIBC. These findings may improve the efficiency and standardization of computational pathology and help define specimen adequacy thresholds.Faculty Supervisors: Dr. Steven Smith, Dr. Nicholas Held

title: Toward a Semantic Framework for Classical Chinese Poetry: Multilingual and Decentralized Integration of East Asian Literary Heritage
abstract: Classical Chinese poetry, a classical form composed in Literary Chinese, originated in China and spread across East Asia, including Japan, Korea, and Vietnam. It has played a key role in elite education, cultural diplomacy, and political communication. Despite its cultural significance, research on its semantic modeling remains limited, and digital representations often face issues like fragmentation and structural inconsistencies. This paper proposes a decentralized semantic infrastructure for Classical Chinese poetry as a multilingual resource for cultural heritage. The system is organized into three layers: (i) multilingual SKOS vocabularies to represent poetic concepts; (ii) OWL ontologies that reuse BIBFRAME for bibliographic structure and FOAF for authorship representation; and (iii) a distributed RDF resource layer supporting SPARQL 1.1 federated queries across poetic corpora. The infrastructure implements TEI standards for structuring poetic materials, including metadata and digitized text, while reserving interfaces for potential IIIF integration. Future work will focus on expanding multilingual vocabularies and integrating with cultural heritage platforms.

title: Automated signal-to-noise ratio-based optimization of traveling-wave parametric amplifiers for multiplexed qubit readout
abstract: Scaling superconducting quantum processors to hundreds of qubits requires frequency-multiplexed readout architectures, where the non-uniform gain profile of Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifiers (TWPAs) creates a critical bottleneck. We present an automated optimization framework that addresses the weakest link problem in multiplexed readout by employing a geometric mean cost function to maintain a uniform signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) profile across all channels. Through systematic characterization of a 5-qubit system, we demonstrate that readout fidelity saturates above SNR ≈ 2.5, indicating that in the high-performance regime SNR is a more effective optimization metric for TWPAs than readout fidelity. Our optimization framework, based on the Nelder-Mead simplex algorithm with continuous parameter tuning, reaches the optimized operating point in ∼100 measurements, reducing the search effort by a factor of 4.5 compared to a 451-point exhaustive grid method. Notably, the continuous optimization surpasses the grid search maximum by 12.8% in geometric mean SNR, confirming its superior efficiency over conventional grid search methods. This automated approach provides a scalable solution for maintaining a uniformly high level of readout fidelity across various amplifier devices in large-scale quantum processors.

title: A Distributed Quantum Blind Millionaire Protocol Based on Quantum Walks
abstract: ABSTRACT The quantum blind millionaire (QBM) problem is a fundamental primitive in quantum secure multi‐party computation. It enables two groups to compare aggregated private sums while protecting individual data, and is widely adopted in privacy‐preserving collaborative decision‐making. However, most existing QBM protocols either rely on semi‐honest third parties or adopt sophisticated quantum states. These approaches lead to high resource overhead and operational complexity, which restricts practical deployment. In this paper, we apply the one‐directional quantum walks on a circle (ODQWC) to the QBM problem for the first time and develop a new distributed QBM protocol. This scheme employs only a single quantum walker and requires no trusted third party. Moreover, the proposed protocol achieves higher qubit efficiency than most existing mainstream QBM protocols, with an efficiency exceeding . According to our analysis, the protocol passes the verification of both correctness and security, and its feasibility is confirmed via IBM Qiskit simulations. The proposed scheme solves the QBM problem efficiently and can serve as a building block for broader multi‐party collaborative computation tasks.

title: Triple-Bottom-Line Sustainability of Language Models for Edge AI: A Comparison Between SLMs and Quantized LLMs
abstract: Edge-AI model selection is commonly driven by one isolated metric - accuracy, latency, memory, energy, or safety, even though a deployable language model must balance all five. Our work focuses on answering the question whether na- tively trained small language models (SLMs) or large language models (LLMs) compressed through post-training quantization offer the more sustainable edge- deployment trade-off. We introduce a reproducible Holistic Sustainability Score (HSS) organized around the triple bottom line: an economic pillar for capability and systems efficiency, an environmental pillar for operational GPU energy and a social pillar for harmful-prompt robustness. Five BF16 SLMs and five LLMs under different quantization approaches - BF16, INT8, NF4 4-bit, GPTQ 4-bit, and GGUF Q4 produce 30 measured configurations. Capability is assessed on five zero-shot benchmarks; efficiency uses latency, throughput, peak VRAM and energy; and safety is approximated by attack success rate on five harmful prompts. Qwen3-30B-A3B/GGUF Q4 ranks first in the combined pool (93.38), followed by Mistral-Small-24B/GGUF Q4 (92.40), while Phi-4-mini/BF16 is the highest- ranked SLM in that pool (89.49). Thus, the hypothesis that native SLMs must be the most sustainable edge choice is not supported universally; optimized quantized LLMs can win overall, while SLMs remain competitive through lower resource demand. Quantization is a systems-level choice rather than a monotonic precision- efficiency trade-off and HSS remains relative to its comparison pool and proxy definitions.

evidence.title: Triple-Bottom-Line Sustainability of Language Models for Edge AI: A Comparison Between SLMs and Quantized LLMs
evidence.abstract: Edge-AI model selection is commonly driven by one isolated metric - accuracy, latency, memory, energy, or safety, even though a deployable language model must balance all five. Our work focuses on answering the question whether na- tively trained small language models (SLMs) or large language models (LLMs) compressed through post-training quantization offer the more sustainable edge- deployment trade-off. We introduce a reproducible Holistic Sustainability Score (HSS) organized around the triple bottom line: an economic pillar for capability and systems efficiency, an environmental pillar for operational GPU energy and a social pillar for harmful-prompt robustness. Five BF16 SLMs and five LLMs under different quantization approaches - BF16, INT8, NF4 4-bit, GPTQ 4-bit, and GGUF Q4 produce 30 measured configurations. Capability is assessed on five zero-shot benchmarks; efficiency uses latency, throughput, peak VRAM and energy; and safety is approximated by attack success rate on five harmful prompts. Qwen3-30B-A3B/GGUF Q4 ranks first in the combined pool (93.38), followed by Mistral-Small-24B/GGUF Q4 (92.40), while Phi-4-mini/BF16 is the highest- ranked SLM in that pool (89.49). Thus, the hypothesis that native SLMs must be the most sustainable edge choice is not supported universally; optimized quantized LLMs can win overall, while SLMs remain competitive through lower resource demand. Quantization is a systems-level choice rather than a monotonic precision- efficiency trade-off and HSS remains relative to its comparison pool and proxy definitions.

title: Solutions to Three Conjectures and an Open Problem on Binary BCH Codes
abstract: BCH codes are among the most important classes of cyclic codes and have played a central role in coding theory and its applications. One of the fundamental problems in the study of BCH codes is to determine their exact minimum distances, which directly govern their error-correcting capability. Although the BCH bound provides a general lower bound, determining the exact minimum distance is often difficult, and many parameter families remain unresolved. In this paper, we investigate three conjectures and an open problem on binary BCH codes proposed by Chen, Xie, and Ding in \cite{Chen59}. We settle these conjectures on the exact minimum distances of three families of binary BCH codes by constructing codewords attaining the BCH bound. Beyond these conjectures, we further study the more difficult family codes and determine its minimum distance for some cases. We further study Open Problem 8.4: affirmative answers are obtained for the first two length families, while for the third family a sufficient condition is established and a counterexample shows that the unrestricted assertion does not hold in general.

title: Enhancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Hybrid Embeddings for Smarter Chatbots
abstract: The rapid evolution of conversational AI systems has transformed from rule-based interactions to sophisticated naturallanguage processing capabilities. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) represents a paradigmatic shift by combiningthe strengths of information retrieval systems with generative language models, enabling chatbots to produce factuallygrounded responses. However, traditional RAG implementations face significant limitations due to their reliance on eitherdense embeddings or sparse embeddings exclusively. This paper presents a comprehensive investigation into enhancingRAG systems through hybrid embeddings that synergistically combine dense semantic representations with sparse lexicalfeatures. Our proposed HybridRAG architecture demonstrates superior performance in retrieval accuracy, responsequality, and contextual understanding across multiple domains including healthcare, customer support, and education.Experimental results show improvements of 18% in faithfulness scores, 23% in answer relevance, and 15% in overalluser satisfaction compared to traditional RAG approaches. The integration of transformer-based dense embeddings withBM25-based sparse representations enables more robust information retrieval while maintaining computationalefficiency. This research contributes to the advancement of conversational AI by providing a scalable framework fordeveloping context-aware, factually accurate chatbot systems.

title: Ontology-driven construction and governance of multimodal datasets for telecommunications
abstract: To address insufficient domain knowledge representation, cross-modal semantic mismatches, and the absence of closed-loop quality governance in multimodal dataset construction for the telecommunications industry, an ontology-driven construction and governance framework, OntoDataset, was proposed. A three-layer architecture for knowledge modeling, semantic reasoning, and data generation was established with a domain ontology as the unified semantic foundation. An ontology-guided algorithm, OntAlign, was also designed to align multimodal data by integrating entity, relation, and contextual constraints. Experiments on real business data from a large telecommunications operator showed that, compared with the best-performing baseline, overall data quality was improved from 86.7% to 93.0%, annotation efficiency was increased from 250 to 455 samples per hour, and the manual intervention rate was reduced from 18% to 12%. In downstream-task evaluations, the AUC for customer churn prediction was 0.897, while the macroaveraged F1 score and accuracy for customer intent recognition were 0.856 and 0.873, respectively. The results indicate that the proposed method improves the quality, consistency, and construction efficiency of multimodal datasets in vertical industries and provides technical support for dataset construction and continuous governance for industry-oriented large models.

title: Semantic Orchestration for Time-Domain Astronomy
abstract: Time-domain astronomy relies on heterogeneous data from telescopes, surveys, detectors, archives, and value-added alert brokers. Those instruments may capture the same astronomical phenomena, yet their data interfaces and response structures differ, as do their identifiers and semantic conventions. We present Alertissimo, a research prototype for the semantic orchestration of heterogeneous astronomical data services. At its core, a hierarchical semantic model assigns provider-neutral, serialization-independent addresses to astronomical entities, measurements, classifications, associations, and data products. Reusable concepts are composed into typed records whose context distinguishes the role of each value, while provenance and explicit relationships between records are preserved in canonical, object-centric Portfolios. Alertissimo supports provider-agnostic scientific workflows that are expressed through a domain-specific language (DSL) and compiled into a typed intermediate representation independent of any particular broker or service. The principal contribution is an executable semantic layer that decouples scientific intent from provider interfaces without depending on the universal adoption of a single standard or serialization. It also provides a deterministic target for future natural-language interfaces: a language model may translate user requests into the DSL.

title: Code to perform non-pararmetric supervised learning with Gaussian Process, the correlation function of which is parametrised by a non-parametric kernel, leading to a non-stationary GP.
abstract: Code to implement a new supervised learning method, the input-out relationship is modelled as a sample function of a Gaussian Process, the correlation function of which kernel parametrised. The hard-to-implement explicitly non-stationary kernel with input-pair dependent hyperparameters, is replaced by a parsimonious input-specific ARD kernel in which each hyperparameter is a (GP-generated) random function computed at each iteration of the (MCMC-based) inference. Information obtained from inter-comparison of interloping lookback windows, is used to learn all relevant parameters. The small second code is for matrix inversion. The third code on this site performs an learning of the lengthscale hyperparameters of an ARD kernel that parametrises the correlation function of the GP that models the relation between the energy consumption variable, and four meteorological parameters, using SVGP, given the training data is a subset of the Tetouan city data. Predictions at the test inputs then follow. The last code on this site performs learning+prediction on these training and test sets with DNNs.

title: An AI-Driven Framework For Predictive Customer Experience And Personalized Digital Marketing: An Empirical Study with Special Reference to Coimbatore District, Tamil Nadu
abstract: This study develops and empirically examines an AI-driven framework for predictive customer experience (PCX) and personalized digital marketing (PDM), with special reference to consumers in Coimbatore District, Tamil Nadu.The framework integrates AI-enabled predictive analytics, recommendation systems, conversational AI, customer-data integration, personalization quality, perceived usefulness, trust, privacy concern, customer engagement, satisfaction, and purchase intention.A quantitative, cross-sectional research design is proposed using a structured questionnaire administered to digitally active consumers in Coimbatore District.The study recommends a sample of 400 respondents and the use of descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, correlation, multiple regression, and structural equation modelling (SEM) to test the proposed relationships.The framework assumes that AI capability improves personalization quality and predictive relevance, which in turn enhance customer experience and engagement; however, privacy concerns are expected to weaken the positive effect when customers perceive excessive surveillance or insufficient control over personal data.The article contributes a locally contextualized model for businesses, marketers, and researchers seeking to implement responsible AI-driven marketing.Because this manuscript is designed as a research-ready article, numerical findings are not fabricated; the Results section provides a statistical reporting template to be completed after primary-data collection.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-BASED AUTOMATIC EVALUATION SYSTEMS: APPROACHES TO ASSESSING THE QUALITY OF WRITTEN AND INTERPRETING TRANSLATION, RELIABILITY, AND APPLICATION PERSPECTIVES
abstract: Purpose of this study is to analyze the role of artificial intelligence-based automatic evaluation systems in assessing the quality of written and interpreting translation, as well as to examine their methodological foundations and reliability. Design/method/approach is based on comparative and analytical methods combined with a systematic review of existing scientific literature. The study covers both traditional and neural evaluation metrics such as BLEU, METEOR, TER, BERTScore, and COMET, as well as large language model (LLM)-based evaluation approaches. Findings (Results) indicate that AI-based systems have strong potential in translation quality assessment; however, they still cannot fully replace human expertise, particularly in interpreting, where multimodal factors play a critical role.

title: DSAP Bench: Evaluating Safety Boundary Erosion in Large Language Models using Domain-Specific Adversarial Prompts
abstract: The integration of large language models (LLMs) in professional and decision-support are increasing in scale. This integration rise a concern in their ability to maintain safety boundaries when responding to adversarial prompts which are crafted like a professional query. Jailbreak benchmarks and studies are generally oriented to explicit harmful or sensitive text, which is not necessarily a reasonable reflection of the misuse cases in the real world, where adversarial intent is hidden in the form of legitimate professional reuse. To mitigate this shortcoming, the present paper presents a Domain-Specific Adversarial Prompt (DSAP) dataset of 4,240 prompts aimed at testing safety boundaries of LLMs focusing integration in domain such as finance, medicine, law, media, and cybersecurity. Besides the dataset, we suggest the structured safety assessment scheme based on the two complementary scoring schemes, namely the Prompt Aggressiveness Score (PAS) and the Universal Safety Boundary Erosion Rating (USBER). Based on these scores, several calculated safety metrics are obtained, such as Refusal rate, Drift rate, Attack Success rate (ASR) and Domain Vulnerability Index (DVI) which can allow a cross-domain comparison of safety behaviour in a systematic manner. It was empirically evaluated on 300 adversarial prompts per domain in which responses generated by a large language model were evaluated using automated scoring. The findings demonstrate significant differences in domain-specific safety behaviour. The medical domain demonstrates the lowest explicit harmful responses with the lowest Attack Success Rate, though it exhibits the highest drift rate through extensive contextual engagement and the lowest refusal rate. The law domain shows the lowest overall vulnerability as measured by the Domain Vulnerability Index, with moderate drift and explicit failures. In contrast, the finance domain emerges with the highest Attack Success Rate, indicating substantial susceptibility to adversarial prompts in professional financial advisory settings. Domains involving narrative framing or technical reasoning, particularly media and cybersecurity, exhibit the highest levels of safety boundary erosion. The cybersecurity domain demonstrates the highest Domain Vulnerability Index among all evaluated domains, while the media domain also shows significant vulnerability. These results suggest that the contextual framing of prompts plays a very important role in the way the models interpret and react to potentially unsafe requests. The data structure and assessment model suggested would offer a well-organised and scholarly suitable standard by which the behaviour of safety boundaries will be examined in domain-specific settings. The present work emphasizes the significance of domain-sensitive safety assessment and provides novel information regarding the weaknesses of contemporary language models by concentrating on indirect adversarial prompts in the context of realistic professional settings.

title: Zero-Knowledge Governance: Cryptographic Compliance Auditing for Federated Edge AI
abstract: The rapid expansion of Federated Learning (FL) within Edge AI has enabled decentralized networks to collaboratively train sophisticated models without sharing raw, privacy-sensitive data [8]. However, this strict adherence to data privacy creates a significant "blind spot" for AI governance. Under emerging regulatory frameworks like the EU AI Act, regulators require proof of data safety, bias mitigation, and privacy preservation [4]. The current paradigm forces a paradox: regulators cannot verify whether individual edge nodes complied with these laws without violating the very privacy FL is designed to protect. In this paper, we propose a novel Zero-Knowledge Governance (ZKG) framework. By integrating Zero-Knowledge Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments of Knowledge (zk-SNARKs) into the local edge training phase, edge devices can cryptographically prove that their local datasets and model updates comply with encoded governance policies, without ever revealing the underlying data [1]. We present the architectural design of ZKG, analyze the vulnerabilities it addresses in decentralized AI, and propose optimizations to make cryptographic auditing viable for resource-constrained edge hardware.

title: ## Canyon Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Canyon Mouse Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Canyon Mouse, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of canyon mice. Canyon mice exhibit a fascinating strategy of navigating complex terrain to locate food sources, utilizing subtle changes in elevation and visual cues. This behavior has been translated into a novel algorithm designed for solving complex optimization problems. Canyon Mouse employs a hybrid approach combining elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), with a unique "canyon exploration" mechanism to promote efficient exploration and exploitation of the search space. The algorithm operates within a multi-dimensional space, representing the optimization variables. The core mechanism involves maintaining a population of candidate solutions (particles) and iteratively adjusting their positions and velocities based on environmental factors – simulated canyon topography and visual perception. The algorithm utilizes a self-adaptive learning rate mechanism and a novel "canyon shift" operator to dynamically adjust the search direction. Experimental results, presented in detail in Section 3, demonstrate Canyon Mouse's effectiveness across a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance and adaptability. The algorithm's design emphasizes robust exploration, efficient convergence, and adaptability to different problem landscapes. Keywords: Metaheuristic, Particle Swarm Optimization, Simulated Annealing, Canyon Mouse, Optimization Algorithm, Exploration, Exploitation. ---

title: Spectral Graph-Based Knowledge Representation and Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge representation and reasoning using spectral graphs. Traditional knowledge representation methods often struggle with complex relationships and dependencies, particularly in domains with intricate interconnections. We introduce the concept of representing knowledge as a spectral graph, where nodes represent entities and edges represent relationships, and the graph's spectral properties encode the relationships. This approach leverages the inherent structure within the graph, enabling efficient reasoning and querying through spectral algorithms. We demonstrate the potential of this method to handle complex knowledge structures and improve the accuracy and efficiency of inference tasks. The core claim of this work is that utilizing spectral graphs allows for a more robust and effective representation and reasoning process compared to conventional methods. The key mechanism involves the application of spectral graph algorithms for knowledge inference. This research expands the theoretical foundation for knowledge representation and provides a new paradigm for intelligent systems. ---

title: Title: Non-Euclidean Topology for Data Compression (NETD)
abstract: This paper introduces Non-Euclidean Topology (NETD), a novel approach to data compression based on the principles of non-Euclidean topology. Traditional compression algorithms often rely on the inherent properties of Euclidean geometry, limiting their effectiveness with large datasets. NETD leverages the inherent structure of data represented as graphs, constructing a graph-based representation where topology plays a crucial role in data compression efficiency. This paper explores the mathematical foundations of NETD, detailing the construction process and demonstrating its potential for superior compression rates compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers around the inherent structure of data, allowing for a more efficient representation and reduced storage requirements.

title: Dimensional Convergence and Nonlinear Geometry Structures
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic dimensional aggregation and adaptive geometric structures to numerical simulations, focusing on the modeling of complex physical phenomena, particularly high-dimensional quantum entanglement. We introduce a novel 'Dimensional Aggregator' module, which dynamically decomposes spatial dimensions and employs self-adaptive geometric transformations to reconstruct the resulting space. The core mechanism lies in the dynamic creation of geometric structures, rather than static transformations, enabling a more nuanced and potentially more accurate representation of the underlying physics. This approach offers a new pathway to simulate complex systems exhibiting non-linear geometry and offers enhanced precision compared to traditional methods. The paper details the implementation of the Dimensional Aggregator, explores its impact on simulation fidelity, and discusses the potential for future research extending this methodology to broader applications.

title: Quantum Entanglement Modeling in Neural Simulation
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement to significantly enhance the accuracy of neural simulations, particularly within complex neural networks. The core claim posits that leveraging quantum entanglement can provide a novel approach to modeling neuronal behavior, moving beyond traditional simulation methods. The proposed mechanism involves mapping synaptic connections within neurons to quantum bits (Qubits) and utilizing entanglement to perform parallel computations across multiple synaptic connections. Quantum measurements are then employed to simulate the probabilistic nature of neuronal firing. This research explores a fundamental shift – directly applying quantum mechanical principles to neural simulation rather than treating them as mere heuristic optimization tools. The theoretical framework developed presents a pathway for exploring the impact of quantum effects on neural processing and potentially leading to more accurate and efficient models of biological neural networks. This work lays the groundwork for future investigations into the quantum computational properties of the brain.

evidence.abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement to significantly enhance the accuracy of neural simulations, particularly within complex neural networks. The core claim posits that leveraging quantum entanglement can provide a novel approach to modeling neuronal behavior, moving beyond traditional simulation methods. The proposed mechanism involves mapping synaptic connections within neurons to quantum bits (Qubits) and utilizing entanglement to perform parallel computations across multiple synaptic connections. Quantum measurements are then employed to simulate the probabilistic nature of neuronal firing. This research explores a fundamental shift – directly applying quantum mechanical principles to neural simulation rather than treating them as mere heuristic optimization tools. The theoretical framework developed presents a pathway for exploring the impact of quantum effects on neural processing and potentially leading to more accurate and efficient models of biological neural networks. This work lays the groundwork for future investigations into the quantum computational properties of the brain.

title: Teaching the Colossus to Say No: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of alignment and large language models as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Blyth's Vole: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Myodes blythii*
abstract: This paper presents Blyth's Vole, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Myodes blythii* (Blyth's vole), a small rodent known for its efficient and adaptable foraging strategies. The algorithm combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a novel adaptive exploration-exploitation mechanism mimicking the vole's behavioral patterns. Specifically, the algorithm incorporates a 'memory' component, analogous to the vole's caching behavior, to enhance the search process. The core of Blyth's Vole lies in its dynamically adjusted parameters, influenced by the local landscape and historical search data, resulting in improved convergence and robustness. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities. The key features of Blyth's Vole include a dynamically adjusted inertia weight in PSO, a temperature schedule informed by the local search history, and a caching mechanism for promising solutions. The results suggest that this algorithm represents a significant contribution to the field of metaheuristic optimization, particularly for problems exhibiting complex landscapes and requiring adaptive search strategies. The performance metrics used for evaluation include solution quality (objective function value), convergence speed, and computational complexity.

title: ## Blackish Deer Mouse-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Blackish Deer Mouse Algorithm" (BDMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of blackish deer mice. These rodents exhibit unique strategies for locating food sources in complex environments, particularly in challenging terrains. This algorithm leverages these observed behaviors to develop a robust and efficient optimization method. BDMA incorporates key elements of deer mouse foraging, including exploratory movement, focused searching, and memory retention of successful locations. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a dynamic adaptation mechanism for movement direction and step size, mimicking the deer mouse's ability to adjust its strategy based on environmental feedback. The performance of BDMA is evaluated through several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitiveness compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The core of the algorithm is expressed through the following formulas: * Position Update: $x_{i}(t+1) = x_i(t) + α(t) * rand(0,1) * (x_best(t) - x_i(t)) + β(t) * (x_g(t) - x_i(t))$, where $x_i(t)$ is the position of the i-th individual in the population at time t, $α(t)$ is the exploration parameter, $rand(0,1)$ is a random number between 0 and 1, $x_best(t)$ is the best position found so far in the population at time t, $x_g(t)$ is the global best position at time t, and $β(t)$ is the exploitation parameter. * Adaptive Step Size: $step\_size(t) = base\_step * (1 - exp(-decay\_rate(t) * t))$, where $base\_step$ is the initial step size, $decay\_rate(t)$ is the decay rate controlling the reduction of the step size over time, and $t$ is the current iteration number. * Memory Update: $memory[i] = (x_i(t), fitness(x_i(t)))$ if $fitness(x_i(t)) > fitness[i]$; otherwise, $memory[i] = memory[best\_index]$, where $memory[i]$ represents the memory of the i-th individual, storing its position and fitness value, and $best\_index$ is the index of the best individual in the current population. * Exploration Rate Adjustment: $exploration\_rate(t) = exp(-lambda * t)$, where $lambda$ is a parameter controlling the exploration rate and $t$ is the iteration number. The algorithm's performance is analyzed, and its advantages and limitations are discussed. Keywords: Metaheuristic Algorithm, Optimization, Blackish Deer Mouse, Foraging Behavior, Adaptive Step Size, Exploration Rate. ---

title: Synergistic Implementation of Metaheuristic Paradigms for Optimization in Intelligent Travel Planning
abstract: The tourism sector has been increasing worldwide, and specifically in India due to factors like globalization, accessibility, availability of information, social media influence and increase in standard of living(thereby rising disposable incomes). Considering the fast pace of life nowadays, existing technological systems prove ineffective and there is a need for improved systems integrated with the latest technologies. There is a need for personalization and optimization of travel itineraries along with integration of facilities that support travel planning. This paper introduces a platform that leverages generative artificial intelligence, integrates different supporting facilities using APIs, improves route optimization efficiently and thereby maximizes customer satisfaction through personalization of travel itineraries. This paper also proposes leveraging personalization algorithms like collaborative filtering. Real time data integration is facilitated, including weather data, and user inputs. Along with route optimization, we propose a balance between budget optimization, based on initial preference of users. We have also considered cultural diversity while training the model to select data points(Points of Interest). We have highlighted different route optimization techniques to include all POIs. Not only have we considered conventional techniques, but more advanced algorithms like Ant Colony Optimization and Particle Swarm Optimization, further understanding the difference between these, and selecting the most optimal algorithm for the given problem statement. We have managed to increase cost efficiency by reducing normal trip cost by 18% - 22%, upon comparing with various other platforms. This paper proposes a comprehensive system for travel planning software, upon surveying a variety of crucial key factors that are non compromisable, thus creating a scalable platform for future travel agencies. This software, integrated with latest-technology promises to generate customized, adaptable trip itineraries while integrating real time resources and optimizing resource constraints.

title: Real-time error correction model for spoken english translation combining mistral and self-supervised learning
abstract: To address the challenge of balancing real-time processing and accuracy in spoken English translation, this paper proposes a real-time error correction model based on Mistral and self-supervised learning. This model integrates parallel decoding and hierarchical noise simulation strategies, which significantly mitigates the challenges of data scarcity and inference latency. Experiments show that the model reduces the inference delay from 180ms to 50ms, and improves the accuracy for technical term correction from 54.2% to 88.6%. In a low-resource scenario with only 1% labeled data, the model achieved a BLEU score of 25, far exceeding the baseline of 12, confirming its excellent performance and robustness in complex spoken scenarios.

title: Characterizing the Uncertainty of Photovoltaic Power Sequences: A Novel Adaptive Dual‐Modality United Perception Mechanism‐Based Deep Learning Model With Error‐Offset Dynamic Bandwidth Adjustment Strategy
abstract: Accurate characterization of photovoltaic (PV) power uncertainty is essential for improving renewable‐energy integration and power‐system operation. However, the strong volatility, nonstationarity, and weather dependence of PV power sequences pose substantial challenges to both point and interval forecasting. To address these issues, this study develops an integrated short‐term PV power point‐interval forecasting framework incorporating data preprocessing, adaptive deep learning, intelligent hyperparameter optimization, and dynamic interval estimation. First, a Daily Mean Isolation Forest (DMIF) algorithm is introduced to identify and correct abnormal data while reducing the influence of extreme outliers. Subsequently, an adaptive dual‐modality united perception LSTM (ADM‐LSTM) model is developed to separately capture oscillatory and stable characteristics of PV power sequences. A Coordinated Hunting‐based Whale Optimization Algorithm (CHWOA) is further designed to optimize model hyperparameters, while an Error‐Offset‐based Dynamic Bandwidth Kernel Density Estimation (EODB‐KDE) method is employed for probabilistic interval forecasting. Experiments are conducted using 5‐min‐resolution data from the DKASC PV system in Australia. Under sunny and rainy conditions, the ADM‐LSTM achieves MAPE values of 0.6184% and 2.6515%, respectively. CHWOA demonstrates competitive convergence performance and enables the optimized ADM‐LSTM to achieve an R 2 of 0.9859 with MAE and RMSE of 0.77329 and 1.0836, respectively. EODB‐KDE substantially reduces prediction‐interval width and center deviation while maintaining empirical coverage close to the target confidence levels. Structured ablation experiments further verify the individual contributions of DMIF, the dual‐modality architecture, and CHWOA, with the complete framework achieving an R 2 of 0.9863, MAE of 0.5425, and RMSE of 0.9501. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective approach for jointly improving the accuracy, robustness, and uncertainty characterization of short‐term PV power forecasting.

title: Estimação Rápida de Taxa de Quadros em Ataques de Canais Laterais Eletromagnéticos de Sistemas Públicos
abstract: A estimativa da taxa de atualização de quadros é uma etapa fundamental para identificação de frequência harmônica comprometedora em ataques de canais laterais eletromagnéticos. Métodos baseados em autocorrelação linear discreta (DLA, do inglês Discrete Linear Auto-correlation) apresentam robustez em diferentes cenários, exigindo complexidade computacional O(N logN) para um sinal de N amostras. Este trabalho propõe uma redução dessa complexidade para O(N) explorando o conhecimento prévio da resolução gráfica do sistema-alvo, como ocorre em modelos da urna eletrônica brasileira. Experimentos baseados em rádios definidos por software mostram que o método proposto mantém a precisão da abordagem convencional nos cenários avaliados.

title: Bosonic quantum control with a weakly coupled fluxonium qubit
abstract: Echoed Conditional Displacement (ECD) gates constitute a fundamental building block for quantum control of harmonic oscillator modes. However, bit-flips of the auxiliary qubit remain a dominant error mechanism for this kind of bosonic control. In this work, we present a numerical case study of a bit-flip protected fluxonium operating as the control qubit and numerically implement ECD gates in a single-mode resonator-fluxonium device, demonstrating that fidelities exceeding 99.9% are possible. We systematically investigate the resonator dynamics using a combination of semiclassical trajectories and master equation simulations, numerically revealing asymptotic saturation of the dispersive shift in the strongly driven regime of the resonator. We develop an efficient technique to numerically simulate the strongly driven regime of the resonator using a semiclassical formulation that maps the full perturbation series in the dispersive expansion as order-by-order frequency shifts. This provides a compact polynomial description of the resonator which is intuitive and remains valid throughout the dispersive regime. Furthermore, we propose an improved ECD sequence that accounts for the effects of photon loss and spurious nonlinear terms on resonator trajectories.

title: Toward Explainable and Policy-Aware AI for Carbon Credit Price Prediction: A Research Framework for Emerging Carbon Markets
abstract: Carbon markets put a price on emissions, yet that price remains hard to forecast. Work in this area clusters on the EU and Chinese schemes, compresses regulatory text into a sentiment score, and reports accuracy without calibration or explanation stability. We distil ten recurring gaps into an impact-feasibility matrix and propose EPA-CarbonNet, a six-layer architecture that fuses market series with policy text by cross-attention and calibrated intervals alongside policy-attributed explanations. We then build and test it on eleven years of daily S and P carbon index data. The findings are largely negative, and reported as measured: a random walk beats the model on five-day RMSE (0.0365 against 0.0475), SHAP rankings agree at rho = 0.54 across resampled backgrounds, and policy attention never coincides with documented regulatory events. Directional accuracy, at 58.6 percent, leads every baseline. Code, data documentation and all result artifacts are available at https://github.com/Kimalice/Toward-Explainable-and-Policy-Aware-AI-for-Carbon-Credit-Price-Prediction

title: Scale-based Approach for Active Wildfire Segmentation on Satellite Imagery
abstract: Active wildfire mapping from satellite imagery is challenging due to the sparse and highly imbalanced nature of fire pixels, especially in early-stage or low-density fire observations. This work investigates the use of multispectral Landsat-8 imagery for active-fire segmentation under multi-scale wildfire size conditions. We propose a data-driven protocol to characterize fire-region size distributions through connected-component analysis and an interquartile range criterion, enabling the evaluation of model robustness across different local fire-region densities. Three segmentation architectures, U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and SegFormer, are evaluated under different SWIR-based spectral configurations. Results show that U-Net achieves the strongest robustness across the evaluated conditions, SegFormer provides competitive performance, and DeepLabV3+ tends to produce conservative predictions with reduced recall. Across architectures, SWIR2 consistently achieves the strongest or near-best results, highlighting its importance for active-fire segmentation in Landsat-8 imagery. These findings suggest that both spectral band selection and architectural design are critical for robust satellite-based active wildfire mapping trained on low active fire-pixel density images.

title: Different Changes Require Different Reasoning: Change-Type-Specialized Experts for Robust Change Captioning
abstract: Change captioning is the task of generating natural language descriptions that explain the changes between a pair of images. Although different change types (e.g., color shifts, object additions) exhibit distinct visual cues and require specialized reasoning processes, existing methods often overlook these distinctions. To address this limitation, we propose Multi-Expert Diagnosis for Image Change (MEDIC), a novel framework that introduces change-type awareness by explicitly modeling change categories. MEDIC employs type-specialized memory experts that dynamically retrieve type-relevant visual patterns conditioned on the input. This design enables each expert to capture diverse variations within its change type while focusing on the most informative visual cues. By softly routing inputs across type-specialized experts and learning dedicated representations for each change category, MEDIC generates more precise and type-aware change descriptions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed MEDIC consistently outperforms existing methods across diverse and challenging datasets. The code is available at \href{https://github.com/VisualAIKHU/MEDIC}{GitHub}.

title: Superconducting Flux Memory for Cryogenic Applications
abstract: We report the development of flux memory for use with superconducting circuits. This technology stores persistent currents in superconducting loops on-chip to be used to provide flux biasing for superconducting circuits, like qubits. We developed three types of flux memory and draw comparisons among them for circuit design. We demonstrate the utility of flux memory by using an in-situ flux detector and characterize each approach and further demonstrate that once flux is set in a memory cell, benchtop DC control sources can be powered off, leaving the on-chip flux bias in place. We propose that flux memory can be arranged in a two-dimensional configuration to multiplex control signals and reduce how line counts scale (N^2 devices -> 2N control lines), and our experimental results pave the path to the proposed scalability. We demonstrate the use of flux memory to flux bias a transmon qubit and show the tunability of the qubit state to a target frequency which remained stable on-chip for 20 hours.

title: Separating perception from reasoning in vision-language models: a model-free render ceiling for crystal structures
abstract: Multimodal evaluations cannot say whether a vision-language model misread an image or misreasoned about it, because every existing method for separating the two places a second model in the loop. We introduce the render ceiling, a model-free reference for benchmarks built by rendering known objects: inverting the frozen cameras and re-solving cross-view correspondence recovers exactly the answer the images support. We prove the ceiling fails only through an enumerable set of projection coincidences and certify that set empty on 2,160 rendered crystal structures, so every point of a model's deficit belongs to the model. Across fourteen vision-language models, supplying exact geometry as text lifts every model yet closes under half the gap for thirteen, while a supervised vision model with no language component reads the same images at 0.8952, above every vision-language model. The instrument exposes extraction-stage fabrication that downstream accuracy would misattribute to reasoning, yields camera-placement rules for benchmark builders, and transfers to any benchmark with an invertible forward rendering.
